Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old woman with history of asthma and peanut allergy presented with acute upper lip swelling and difficulty breathing approximately 30 minutes after ingesting prawn soup; likely anaphylaxis—ambulance called for emergency care.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling of upper lip and difficulty breathing after eating prawn soup.
- Timeline:
    - Ate prawn soup around 7 PM.
    - Noticed lip swelling (left upper lip) about 30 minutes after ingestion; swelling has progressively worsened.
    - Reports “really pumping blood” sensation; swelling increasing.
- Associated symptoms: Difficulty breathing (currently feels she "can't breathe that well"), possibly chest tightness, dizziness.
- Precipitating/relieving factors: Onset occurred after eating prawns; no mention of relief measures taken prior to consult.
- Previous episodes: At least one similar episode a year ago after eating out (unclear exact trigger, possibly curry); had swelling and breathing difficulty next morning.
- Systems review: No additional systems reviewed; no other symptoms specifically related or excluded.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma: Uses salbutamol inhaler regularly; no other inhalers.
- Peanut allergy: Known since childhood; required hospital treatment and "injection" for severe reaction at age six.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Antihistamines (type, dose/route/frequency not documented; patient unsure which ones, uses occasionally).
- Allergies: Peanut.

Social History:
- Goes out to eat with friends; no details on smoking, alcohol (except mention of being "quite drunk" during past reaction), or substance use.
- Lives with mother or mother present at home.

Family History:
- Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- No findings or vital signs documented.

Investigations:
- None mentioned.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute upper lip swelling and respiratory difficulty after prawn ingestion—suspected anaphylaxis.
    - Immediate call for ambulance and advised urgent hospital evaluation.
    - Recommended taking antihistamine while awaiting emergency services.
    - Instructed family to call emergency services ("999"), report suspected anaphylactic reaction, and remain with patient.
    - Emphasis on urgency due to worsening symptoms and history of severe allergy.
- Issue 2: Ongoing asthma and confirmed food allergies.
    - After discharge, advised to contact clinic for follow-up and potential prescription of emergency injections (e.g., epinephrine autoinjector), as references to prior childhood use and need for ongoing management.

General Plan items:
- None additional specified.

Quality checks:

●	Missing elements: Thorough medication reconciliation (specific antihistamine and inhaler details), allergies beyond peanuts, full review of systems, vital signs, physical exam findings.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, relevant history captured; minimal extraneous content; all decision points evident.
